title: Processes & Troubleshooting
pedagogicalStatus: Unreviewed draft: formative practice only; CEFR mastery disabled.

sources.title: Pendulum-video playback note (reading; practice)
paragraphs: On Monday, Nora was watching a classroom video of a pendulum. She was counting the swings when the video stopped at 12 seconds. The video player was not moving, but her notebook was open. First, she checked whether the video was paused. Then she pressed Play again. The video continued, and she finished counting. She wrote a note: “The video stopped while I was counting.” This was a video-learning activity, not a physical experiment.

sources.title: Virtual circuit software note (reading; practice)
paragraphs: Yesterday, Amir was using a circuit simulation. He was drawing a graph of current against voltage when the program stopped responding. The virtual source displayed 4.0 V at that moment. Amir did not touch real electrical equipment. He saved his notes, closed the unresponsive simulation, and opened a saved copy. After that, he checked the graph again. He did not claim that the displayed value came from a physical meter.

sources.title: Optics drawing problem (reading; practice)
paragraphs: At 10:15 a.m., Layla was editing a ray diagram on her computer. While she was moving a virtual lens, a label disappeared from the screen. She checked the list of visible layers. The label was hidden, not deleted. She turned the label layer on and continued her drawing. Later, she told her partner what had happened. No laser or real lens was used.

sources.title: Temperature model log (reading; practice)
paragraphs: On Thursday, a group was watching a virtual temperature display. The timer was running, but the number on the screen was not changing. The display still showed 22.0 °C. While one student was reading the help panel, another student noticed that the model was paused. They resumed the simulation and observed the display change to 23.0 °C. They were using a model; no hot material was handled.
